maturity_time.meaning: maturityTime[msg.sender], the lock-up maturity timestamp for the withdrawing staker (uninitialized mapping entry)

maturity_check_present.meaning: GaugeV2._withdraw contains the block.timestamp >= maturityTime[msg.sender] maturity check

never_initialized.meaning: maturityTime mapping is never initialized or updated anywhere in GaugeV2

deposit_capable.meaning: the staker can deposit tokens into GaugeV2 before the withdrawal

withdraw_completed.meaning: the staker's _withdraw call completes and returns the deposited tokens

preconditions.text: GaugeV2._withdraw contains the maturity check on maturityTime[msg.sender]; maturityTime is never initialized or updated, so as an uninitialized uint256 mapping it equals 0 for the withdrawing staker; block.timestamp is greater than 0; and the staker can deposit tokens beforehand.
preconditions.derivation: Conjunction of extracted preconditions: p_lockup_check (maturity_check_present), p_mapping_uninitialized (never_initialized), p_maturity_zero supported by p_default_zero (maturity_time == 0), p_timestamp_positive (block_timestamp > 0), p_deposit (deposit_capable).

safety.text: Withdrawal completion is authorized only when an actual maturity lock-up is in force, i.e., maturityTime[msg.sender] is a nonzero future timestamp (maturity_time > 0); the maturity check must not allow completion without an established lock-up.
safety.derivation: si_enforce_lockup requires the maturity check to enforce the intended lock-up/vesting period; enforcing a lock-up presupposes a real nonzero maturity for the user, so withdraw_completed implies maturity_time > 0. The trivially satisfied block.timestamp >= maturityTime direction is not asserted as the whole wish.

effects.text: The staker's _withdraw completes while maturityTime[msg.sender] equals 0, so no maturity lock-up is in force and the intended lock-up is bypassed.
effects.derivation: i_instant_withdraw reports deposited tokens can be withdrawn immediately in the same transaction/block, bypassing the lock-up; this is withdraw_completed together with no lock-up in force, i.e. not(maturity_time > 0), which falsifies the safety property.

effect_coverage.reason: Formalized as withdraw_completed AND not(maturity_time > 0): immediate withdrawal occurs while maturityTime[msg.sender] is 0, bypassing the lock-up.

assumptions: a_intended_maturity: maturityTime was intended to be set to a nonzero future timestamp when a user stakes, but the implementation omitted this.
The withdrawing staker is the msg.sender evaluated by the maturity check in _withdraw.
unresolved: Where and when maturityTime was supposed to be assigned is unspecified, so the intended lock-up duration cannot be quantified.
The staking/deposit function name and any authorization requirements for _withdraw are not given.

limitations: i_flash_staking (potential flash-staking reward attack) is a downstream/potential impact and is not formalized in this claim.
Impacts are asserted capabilities, not a verified on-chain incident.
No token or reward value at risk is quantified; economic impact is out of scope.
Reward accrual and claimability within the same block are not detailed.
The intended lock-up duration and the assignment site of maturityTime are unspecified.
